# Sort

Sorts the elements of an array in ascending order.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
Sort(items)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | array | The array to sort, which is left unchanged. Null is read as the empty array; any other type that is not an array is a runtime error. |

## Returns

Array. A new array holding the elements of items in ascending order. Never null.

## Remarks

Values of different types never cause an error: null comes first, then booleans, numbers, strings, arrays, objects and functions. Booleans sort false before true, numbers by value, and strings by their UTF-16 code units, so case counts and upper-case letters come before lower-case ones. Two arrays, or two objects, compare equal: their contents are not compared. The sort is stable: elements that compare equal keep their original order.

## Example

`Sort([3, 1, 2])` returns `[1, 2, 3]`.

`Sort(["b", null, 1])` returns `[null, 1, "b"]`.
